item.title: What the collapse of a $2 billion law firm reveals
item.description:
Weil, Gotshal & Manges was a nearly century-old law firm that was profitable, prestigious and apparently healthy — until an exodus of superstar partners caused it to unravel.
In the wake of the firm's collapse, host Megan McArdle talks with legal journalist David Lat about workplace loyalty, the “businessification” of professions and the power of top employees. They also explore how AI is eliminating the entry-level tasks that once trained young lawyers and what happens across industries when technology removes the first rung of the career ladder.
